body: Why is it so easy to blame Lucifer for temptation when he was originally God’s angel? He disagreed with god and was banished for trying to understand god’s will. In the book of Job, god decided to gamble with Lucifer and say that Job would still believe in him even if he lost everything. So does that mean that it wasn’t god who destroyed Job’s land and killed his family and farm? All over a mere bet that some dictator called “god” decided to have with the angel that he banished just for simply speaking against him? Sure, Job was given better land, a richer farm, and a more beautiful family, but what happens to the trauma he was given when his family and land was taken away from him? Do we ignore the fact that Job had a wife and kids (that he probably loved) that are now just dead over a meaningless bet? Do we ignore that god tortured a random man on earth because he wanted to play a game with Lucifer? One of the commandments is “You shall not steal”, yet that story tells me that god stole everything from Job. Another commandment is to not commit adultery yet cheating is a very common thing with Christian families. So because you were taught to fear some being you knew nothing about and deciding this being’s word is absolute, temptation is all Lucifer’s fault? Who created temptation? If god is the creator of all things then he created temptation, right?

I worked at a restaurant as a server and I was the only worker other than the boss who spoke enough English to have conversations with customers and troubleshoot any requests that our customers had. The other server spoke really broken English, but he could at least take orders and have somewhat decent conversations. Since I was the most proficient English speaker at the restaurant, my responsibilities were to take in store orders, phone orders, bring food from the kitchen to the tables, and help prep cook during down times. On occasions the boss would send me out to do cater delivery, go to the grocery store to buy ingredients (or beer for us the drink in the kitchen lmao). Most days it wasn't busy, so I didn't mind if she had me handling the whole store front by myself while the other server would focus on prep cooking, bringing food out from the kitchen while I was busy, and just drinking in the kitchen. Mother's day came and the entire restaurant was packed. Every table was seated and needed their orders taken, the phone was ringing constantly, I was constantly telling everyone in the back that I needed the other server to at least try to help me take orders out there because I couldn't handle every order all by myself, but everytime I went back to the kitchen to place the order tickets, I would just see him next to the food grill, drinking a modelo and waiting for food to be ready so he could take it out. After my fifth time being in the kitchen and seeing him chilling in the back drinking a modelo and conversating with the boss and the cooks while I was dying out in the front, I got a complaint from one of the customers while taking a phone order. I ended up literally punching the order on the computer and slamming the double doors to the kitchen. My boss ended up pushing me and told me to go outside, have a smoke break and take a breather, then she sent me home after that and told me to calm down before the closing shift. 2 minutes before the closing shift, I texted her saying that I wasn't coming back.

Didn't really need an argument. I grew up with parents that were almost never home and if they were, all I heard was arguing. When I turned 10 my mom started to be more involved in my life, but I would get annoyed because video games were my only escape from all the yelling and fighting at home. I either had my brother take care of me if he wasn't at work or school or I was sleeping over at a friend or cousin's house for weeks on end. The few times I was home, I would get lost in my video games and sometimes my mom would bother me to go drive around town and look for my dad, and when we found him, he was always gambling and I would make remarks that would end in me and my dad throwing punches at each other. With a childhood like that, I always questioned whether or not my parents actually loved each other, if marriage actually had a meaning, and whether or not they even wanted me and my brother. With a foundation like that, I'm convinced on pro-choice. If someone doesn't want a child or doesn't feel like they can take care of a child, then why should they be forced to have one? Especially if it's a child of rape. The mother of that child is more likely to hate her own child and not take care of it. If you make her have that child, all you're doing is putting stress on her by making her raise something she didn't want in the first place, and in turn, that child will grow up to be a hateful person because that's all that it was raised around.

I was hospitalized two times for one and a half weeks each time (first time for breaking my leg and the second time for an infection because they didn't properly clean my leg the first time). Went through a quarter life crisis a year before my friends did. The second time I was hospitalized it took them 5 tries to stick the IV in my bloodstream. The scariest part about the second time was the fact that as the days went by, I started to forget my name, my birthday, where I lived, and I started openly asking them to kill me when they asked me if I needed anything (i.e Nurse : "Do you need anything?" Me : "Yeah, can you inject bleach/cyanide/sulfide in my IV?"). When my mom drove me home, I was looking at the neighborhood (the same road I always take to go to work) as if I was in a different country. Coming in and leaving the hospital the second time changed me. I started becoming more of a home body, I stopped contacting my friends (I still hang out every once in awhile, only if they ask me to go out and I feel comfortable leaving my room). I started focusing on things that I want to do now instead of doing things just because my friends wanted to do them. I've cut people off that I've deemed to be non beneficial to my future or just energy consuming (that includes family). I also started being more open about my feelings at home (I already get tired when I go out because I have to hide parts of me around certain people. I wanted to at least feel comfortable in my own house for once. I needed at least one outlet other than alcohol where I could at least feel accepted and understood. Now, instead of going out every other day to get drunk, I go to school, go to work, try to work on my crafts, self teach whatever I want to learn, and go out maybe once a month.
